Skewness of the Modified Half-Normal Distribution

Source: R/mhn_moments.R
mhn_skewness.Rd

Computes the skewness \(\gamma_1 = E[(X - \mu)^3] / \sigma^3\) for \(X \sim \mathrm{MHN}(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)\).

Usage

mhn_skewness(alpha, beta, gamma)

Arguments

alpha

Shape parameter (\(\alpha > 0\)), a single number.

beta

Rate-type parameter (\(\beta > 0\)), the coefficient of the Gaussian tail \(\exp(-\beta x^2)\); larger values pull mass toward zero. A single number.

gamma

Tilt parameter (\(\gamma \in R\)), the coefficient of the exponential tilt \(\exp(\gamma x)\). A single number.

Value

A numeric scalar.

Details

The central moments are obtained by numerical integration against the unnormalised density, in a variable centred on its peak (or, where the density decreases from the origin, on a logarithmic scale), so no normalising constant is needed. Building them from raw moments by the Lemma 2b recurrence from the mean of Lemma 2a is exact algebra but cancels once the standard deviation is small next to the mean, which is what a large tilt produces; that expansion is used only where the integration cannot be set up.

Against independent quadratures, for shapes from 1 to 60 and tilts \(\gamma / \sqrt{\beta}\) from -20 to 12, the absolute error stayed below 1e-9; the largest found, 3e-10, is for a shape between 2 and 3 under a positive tilt.

For a subnormal shape, below the smallest normal double 2.2e-308, the moments are taken from forms in which the shape only multiplies (see the Details of dmhn). While the mass at the peak is small against the mass by the origin (\(w\) well below 1, up to a tilt \(z = \gamma / \sqrt{\beta}\) of about 53 at the largest subnormal shape and 54.5 at the smallest), the skewness then grows like \(1 / \sqrt{\alpha}\) as the shape falls, by a factor that depends on the tilt: 1.25 at \(z = 0\) and \(2.8 \times 10^{-8}\) at \(z = 12\). It turns negative where \(w\) is about 1 (\(z\) from about 53.3 to 54.7), and past the tilt where the forms hand over (55 to 56.3) it no longer depends on \(\alpha\).

The function is not vectorised in its parameters: alpha, beta and gamma must each be a single number. To evaluate several parameter triples, use mapply, as in the examples.

References

Sun, J., Kong, M., & Pal, S. (2023). The Modified-Half-Normal distribution: Properties and an efficient sampling scheme. Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods, 52(5), 1591–1613. (Lemmas 2a and 2b)

See also

mhn_kurtosis, mhn_mean

Examples

mhn_skewness(alpha = 2, beta = 1, gamma = 0)
#> [1] 0.6311107
mapply(mhn_skewness, alpha = c(0.5, 2, 5), beta = 1, gamma = c(-1, 0, 3))
#> [1] 1.8814298 0.6311107 0.1579617
